A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Top-H research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, temperature and parameter analyses, runtime measurements, LLM-judge scores, and a human evaluation involving 14 participants.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds Mirostat comparisons, GPQA parameter-sensitivity results, and additional large-model judge scores.

M1.justification: The entropy-constrained objective, descending-probability greedy selection, and stopping rule remain unchanged. V2 Algorithm 2 reproduces incremental entropy accumulation already provided in v1 Appendix C.2; it is not a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Alpaca-Eval, MT-Bench, GSM8K, GPQA, creative-story prompts, and the same human-evaluation task. The added comparisons and sensitivity measurements reuse existing task and dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Mirostat changes from a cited alternative in v1 to an evaluated baseline in v2 Appendix C.6, Tables 11–12. It is compared with Top-H on MT-Bench and GPQA across three models and three temperatures. Existing comparator participation is retained.

E3.justification: V2 adds a GPQA experiment sweeping α from 0.10 to 0.90 in steps of 0.05 with LLaMA3.1-8B-Instruct at T=1.5, measuring accuracy and average sampling-pool size. The new Mirostat comparisons specify τ=3. Existing benchmark, judge, and runtime protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 Appendix C.5 adds an α-sensitivity analysis connecting GPQA accuracy with sampling-pool size, supplementing the existing Alpaca-Eval creativity/coherence analysis. The earlier temperature-sensitivity, exhaustive-search optimality, and truncation case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five repetitions for the creative-writing judge evaluations and retain the existing uncertainty-reporting practices. The added Table 8 rows use the same ± format; no new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or increased run counts are reported.

E6.justification: V2 adds supplementary outcomes: Table 10 reports α-dependent GPQA accuracy and pool sizes; Tables 11–12 show Top-H beating Mirostat in all nine MT-Bench settings and seven GPQA settings, with one GPQA tie and one loss. Table 8 adds 70B judge scores at T=1.5. Matched pre-existing results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.4 introduces a Zipf probability assumption, Lemmas 6–9, and Theorem 6 claiming a distribution-dependent additive approximation bound of order O(n^(-α(s-1))). V1 explicitly left formal approximation guarantees beyond scope. The original equivalence, NP-hardness, and termination arguments are substantively retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: the ECMD/ECMM formulation, NP-hardness claim, greedy Top-H decoder, and improved creativity/coherence at high temperatures. The headline improvement of up to 25.63% is unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 adds explicit limitations concerning absent general competitive guarantees and manual α tuning, with adaptive thresholds proposed as future work. Appendix A.4 discusses distribution-dependent applicability, while C.5 interprets larger sampling pools as supporting diversity but generally reducing GPQA accuracy.

D1.justification: V2 removes v1 Appendix E's complete Hugging Face LogitsProcessor listing and integration instructions, including concrete details such as top_n=100 and batch-size-one handling. This substantially reduces implementation information available within the PDF. The repository link and general hardware/software disclosures remain, and Mirostat's τ=3 setting is added.

R1.justification: V2 newly cites Gerlach and Altmann (2013) to motivate the Zipf assumption and expands the associated theoretical positioning. Mirostat was already cited in v1. The new bibliography entry for Brent and Zimmermann formalizes a work already referenced informally in v1, rather than adding a new intellectual source.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized language corrections, moves runtime discussion from Appendix C.2 to Section 6.1.4, and adds theoretical, experimental, limitations, and acknowledgment sections while removing the implementation appendix. Affiliation and conference-header information also change. The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 10–12, expands Table 8, and reformats several retained tables with revised spacing, headers, and emphasis. The runtime table moves into the main text, and existing entropy pseudocode becomes numbered Algorithm 2. Figures 1–6 retain their plotted content, with some relocation.

improvement.justification: The Mirostat comparisons, GPQA sensitivity analysis, and explicit limitations improve empirical coverage and qualification. However, new Appendix A.4 introduces a substantive mathematical defect: Lemma 8's lower bound can exceed H(k)≤log(k), undermining the claimed approximation guarantee that v1 did not assert. Removing the implementation listing also reduces self-contained reproducibility. These empirical benefits and theoretical/reproducibility regressions leave the net quality direction unclear.
